en: So thanks for coming.

en: This talk is called MCP doesn't suck.
zh: 这个演讲的标题是:MCP 并不烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your agent does.

en: My name is Jan Cern.

en: I'm the founder and CEO of Appify.
zh: 我是 Appify 的创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't know if you've seen these ones around here.

en: Maybe I'll zoom here.

speaker: Unknown
en: Didn't quite work out.

speaker: Unknown
en: But anyway, thanks for coming.

speaker: Unknown
en: So as you know, MCP is a standard to securely access tools and resources, right?
zh: 大家知道,MCP 是一个安全访问工具和资源的标准,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, standard for agent-to-tool interaction.
zh: 基本上就是智能体与工具交互的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been introduced by Anthropic about almost two years ago.
zh: 它是 Anthropic 在差不多两年前推出的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, it took the world by storm, right?
zh: 而且实际上,它风靡了全世界,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, last year, MCP became the darling of the AI world.
zh: 去年,MCP 成为了 AI 世界的宠儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a lot of people build their servers.
zh: 很多人构建了自己的服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think like now there's like 10 to 15,000 servers, right?
zh: 我觉得现在大概有 1 万到 1.5 万个服务器,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of clients adopted it.
zh: 很多客户端都采用了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually it became a standard, you know, like used by Claude or ChatGPT to plug tools and connectors to your AI agents.
zh: 而且它实际上成为了一个标准,被 Claude 或 ChatGPT 用来把工具和连接器接入你的 AI 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were so many MCP servers that people had to create registries of MCP servers.
zh: MCP 服务器多到人们不得不创建 MCP 服务器的注册表。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there were so many registries that people had to create even MCP server registry registries.
zh: 而注册表多到人们不得不创建 MCP 服务器注册表的注册表。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty wild times, right?
zh: 相当疯狂的时代,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So when MCP connects agents with tools, everybody loves MCP, right?
zh: 当 MCP 把智能体和工具连接起来时,人人都爱 MCP,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, not exactly.
zh: 呃,不完全是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, especially last year, there have been a lot of hate about MCP.
zh: 实际上,尤其是去年,有很多针对 MCP 的仇恨言论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, for example, Anthropic admits that MCP sucks.
zh: 比如,Anthropic 承认 MCP 很烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: From Teo, MCP is the wrong abstraction.
zh: 来自 Teo:MCP 是错误的抽象。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic is trying so hard to fix MCP.
zh: Anthropic 正在拼命修复 MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: MCP was a mistake.
zh: MCP 是一个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Long live CLIs.
zh: CLI 万岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: MCP is dead in the water.
zh: MCP 已经死在水里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenClaw has shown me that API and CLI will win.
zh: OpenClaw 让我明白 API 和 CLI 会赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a reason I didn't add MCP support to OpenClaw, except via MCPorter MCP to CLI converter.
zh: 我没给 OpenClaw 加 MCP 支持是有原因的,除了通过 MCPorter 这个 MCP 转 CLI 的转换器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, that's interesting.
zh: 哦,这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: MCPs are mostly useless.
zh: MCP 基本上没用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll die on this hill if I have to.
zh: 必要的话我死也要死在这座山上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every MCP could have been a deterministic CLI.
zh: 每个 MCP 本来都可以是一个确定性的 CLI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I'm going to do next year.
zh: 这就是我明年要做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from Gary Tan, who's going to speak today as well, MCP sucks honestly.
zh: 还有今天也会演讲的 Gary Tan 说:说实话,MCP 很烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my god.
zh: 我的天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Peter Levels, thank god MCP is dead.
zh: 还有 Peter Levels:感谢上帝 MCP 死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm like, what's happening?
zh: 所以我就想,这是怎么回事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are everybody hating MCPs, right?
zh: 为什么人人都恨 MCP,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's crazy.
zh: 太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, let's look at the problem, like what are people talking about?
zh: 首先,我们来看看问题是什么,大家在说什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So the most cited problem was like, hey, MCP eats too much context.
zh: 所以被引用最多的问题是，嘿，MCP 吃掉太多上下文了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, that's true.
zh: 而实际上，这是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the first way how agents implemented MCP was very naive, right?
zh: 我是说，智能体实现 MCP 的第一种方式是非常朴素的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They were like, hey, MCP gives you tools, so there is like, if you have 10 MCP servers, it's just like 10 MCP tools, so there's like 100 tools, and agents would register all these tools in the context right away.
zh: 它们是这么想的：嘿，MCP 给你工具，所以，如果你有 10 个 MCP 服务器，就相当于 10 组 MCP 工具，也就是 100 个工具，然后智能体会立刻把所有这些工具注册进上下文里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before you actually even ask any question,
zh: 所以在你真正提出任何问题之前，

speaker: Unknown
en: MCP would already eat 100 tools in your context.
zh: MCP 就已经用 100 个工具占满了你的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe one third of your context would be gone without actually doing any work.
zh: 可能你三分之一的上下文就这么没了，却什么工作都没做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, this is pretty crazy if you think about it, right?
zh: 说实话，你仔细想想这挺疯狂的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you would be calling tools, basically adding to the context.
zh: 然后你去调用工具，基本上就是在往上下文里加东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The results would be added back to the context again.
zh: 结果又会被再次加回上下文里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically, the context would just grow very long and rot over time.
zh: 基本上，上下文就会变得非常长，并随着时间腐烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: You lose accuracy.
zh: 你损失准确性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It costs a lot of money and so on.
zh: 它花很多钱，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very ineffective way how to do that.
zh: 这是一种非常低效的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not the problem of MCP.
zh: 但这不是 MCP 的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the problem of the harness.
zh: 那是 harness 的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at the MCP specification, what it says about how you should design the harness, it says absolutely nothing.
zh: 如果你去看 MCP 规范里关于你该如何设计 harness 的部分，它什么都没说。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's up to the implementation, right?
zh: 这取决于具体实现，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's your job when you're building your agent to make sure you use MCP effectively.
zh: 所以在你构建智能体时，确保有效地使用 MCP 是你的职责。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the problem of the protocol, right?
zh: 这不是协议的问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So what are the solutions of this?
zh: 那么这个问题的解决方案是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So first solution, fairly naive, is like, hey, let's split the context into sub-agents.
zh: 第一个解决方案，相当朴素，就是：嘿，让我们把上下文拆分给子智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if there's some task,
zh: 所以如果有一些任务，

speaker: Unknown
en: You can basically delegate it to a new sub-agent when it's on context.
zh: 你基本上可以在它占用上下文时把它委托给一个新的子智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, it doesn't pollute the main context window.
zh: 这样一来，它就不会污染主上下文窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's great, but you still have to pay money for those tokens.
zh: 我是说，这很好，但你仍然要为那些 token 付钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't go away.
zh: 那笔开销并没有消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problems like before are still around.
zh: 而且之前那些问题依然存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, if the MCP tool returns some sensitive results, like password,
zh: 例如，如果 MCP 工具返回了一些敏感结果，比如密码，

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, it stays in your context and it can be abused by other tool calls or basically like the application, right?
zh: 基本上它会留在你的上下文里，可能被其他工具调用或者应用程序滥用，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, context is a really bad place to pass sensitive value or like large data.
zh: 所以基本上，上下文是一个传递敏感信息或大数据的非常糟糕的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sub-agents only push that problem a little further but still don't remove it.
zh: 子智能体只是把这个问题往后推了一点，但并没有消除它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's the solution number two?
zh: 那么解决方案二是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was end of the last year, I think first Anthropic and then Cursor introduced something which is called Progressive Tool Discovery.
zh: 我记得是去年年底，我记得先是 Anthropic 然后是 Cursor 引入了所谓的渐进式工具发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, it's so simple that it hurts even that people have to do this, but the idea was like, hey, if
zh: 我是说，这简单得让人难受，人们居然还得这么做，但想法是：嘿，如果

speaker: Unknown
en: We put all the tools into the context, it just consumes too much tokens.
zh: 我们把所有工具都放进上下文，它就消耗太多 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how about we put those tools into the context progressively, only when you need them, right?
zh: 那我们不如渐进地把这些工具放进上下文，只在你需要的时候，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, Anthropic in Claude introduced this tool, just called Tool Search Tool.
zh: 比如，Anthropic 在 Claude 里引入了这个工具，就叫 Tool Search Tool。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically, that tool helps you find other tools and only add those to the context when needed, right?
zh: 基本上，这个工具帮你找到其他工具，并且只在需要时才把它们加进上下文，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it kind of makes sense.
zh: 这挺有道理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would you add all the 100 tools in your context all the time if you rarely need them?
zh: 如果你很少用到那 100 个工具，为什么要一直把它们全部放进上下文呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Typically, you just need maybe one or two.
zh: 通常你大概只需要一两个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, this way, you can save a huge amount of context right away, basically.
zh: 而且实际上，这种方式可以立刻节省大量上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Makes it more effective, cheaper, faster to run, and so on.
zh: 让运行更高效、更便宜、更快，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it kind of makes sense, right?
zh: 所以这挺有道理的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So everybody should be doing it, no?
zh: 那大家都应该这么做，不是吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then solution number three, also introduced end of last year by Cloudflare.
zh: 然后是解决方案三，也是去年年底由 Cloudflare 引入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called CodeMode, right?
zh: 它叫 CodeMode，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the big idea is like, hey,
zh: 它的大想法是：嘿，

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's not treat MCP tools as functions like you would have to add to the context, but treat them as a code.
zh: 我们不要把 MCP 工具当作你必须加进上下文的函数，而是把它们当作代码来对待。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually models are really good at writing and analyzing code because they can use tools like grab,
zh: 而且实际上,模型非常擅长编写和分析代码,因为它们可以使用类似 grab 的工具,

speaker: Unknown
en: They can find the right definition.
zh: 它们可以找到正确的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can navigate the code pretty well.
zh: 它们可以很好地导航代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that way, they can navigate also the tool descriptions and information about the tools and so on.
zh: 这样一来,它们也可以导航工具描述以及关于工具的信息等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a pretty simple idea, very straightforward.
zh: 所以这是一个非常简单的想法,非常直接。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's convert tools, MCP tools and servers, into code and treat it as code, right?
zh: 所以让我们把工具、MCP 工具和服务器,转换成代码,并把它当作代码来对待,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty simple but extremely effective, right?
zh: 非常简单但极其有效,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it turns out
zh: 因为事实证明

speaker: Unknown
en: Models are better at writing and calling code than calling tools because tool calling is an artificial construct, basically, that we have to teach the LLMs to do.
zh: 模型在编写和调用代码方面比调用工具更好,因为工具调用基本上是一种人工构造,我们必须教会 LLM 去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't exist in the real world, in real training data.
zh: 它在现实世界中不存在,不在真实训练数据中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those have to be synthesized and put into the model.
zh: 这些数据必须被合成出来并放进模型里。

speaker: Unknown
en: But unfortunately,
zh: 但不幸的是,

speaker: Unknown
en: Even implementation of code mode is very difficult to use.
zh: 即使是 code mode 的实现也非常难用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very tied to their platform.
zh: 它与他们的平台绑定得很紧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not really straightforward.
zh: 而且它并不是真正直接的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not a lot of people are actually using code mode, except for examples.
zh: 所以除了少数示例之外,实际上没有多少人在真正使用 code mode。

speaker: Unknown
en: So still, most agents are living in the dark ages, and they don't support these features, you know, and most MCP clients.
zh: 所以大多数智能体仍然生活在黑暗时代,它们不支持这些功能,你知道的,大多数 MCP 客户端也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a pity because the protocol has evolved a lot, added a lot of new things, but the clients don't support it.
zh: 这很遗憾,因为协议已经发展了很多,增加了很多新东西,但客户端并不支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how are CLIs different?
zh: 那么 CLI 有什么不同呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, why people compare CLIs to MCP?
zh: 你知道,为什么人们拿 CLI 和 MCP 做比较?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, agents never load the full CLI into context.
zh: 实际上,智能体从不把整个 CLI 加载进上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like the agent would explore all the...
zh: 并不是说智能体会去探索所有的……

speaker: Unknown
en: All the commands of the CLI tool, like, find a help and put it in the context.
zh: CLI 工具的所有命令,比如运行 help 然后把它放进上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no.
zh: 不,不。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's doing it progressively by default.
zh: 它默认是渐进式地做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the agent is calling the CLI tool only when needed.
zh: 所以智能体只在需要时才调用 CLI 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes, actually, it knows the tools by heart.
zh: 而且有时候,它其实已经把工具背得滚瓜烂熟了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, so, for example, the basic Linux commands the agents already know because they have seen the training data since, you know, forever.
zh: 比如,例如,基本的 Linux 命令智能体已经知道了,因为它们从,你知道的,很久以前就在训练数据中见过这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also they can, like, learn about the tools, the CLI tools from help because there is help.
zh: 但它们也可以,比如,通过 help 来了解工具,了解 CLI 工具,因为有 help。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually,
zh: 而且实际上,

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents run CLI tools as code by default, right?
zh: 智能体默认把 CLI 工具当作代码来运行,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, in order to run CLI tools, you have to have some runtime, like sandbox or machine that you can run the commands in.
zh: 所以,为了运行 CLI 工具,你必须有某种运行时,比如沙箱或者可以在其中运行命令的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, and when you invoke these CLI tools, I mean, it's code mode by default.
zh: 所以,当你调用这些 CLI 工具时,我的意思是,它默认就是 code mode。

speaker: Unknown
en: You run it as a code.
zh: 你把它当代码来运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like bash code, but it's still code.
zh: 它就像 bash 代码,但它仍然是代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, it's basically like code mode, like, it's available to CLI's from scratch, while MCP only had to, like, sort of, like, grow into it, you know?
zh: 所以,你知道的,它基本上就像 code mode,CLI 从一开始就有这个能力,而 MCP 则是不得不, sort of, 慢慢地长出这个能力,你知道的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is important, like, agents know the shell by heart.
zh: 这一点很重要,智能体把 Shell 背得滚瓜烂熟。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Linux shell, Linux or Unix has been around from, like, 1969, when Ken Thompson and Ritchie actually created Linux.
zh: 我的意思是,Linux shell,Linux 或 Unix 从大约 1969 年就存在了,当时 Ken Thompson 和 Ritchie 实际上创造了 Linux。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you look at the basic terminal, that black box of 80 columns and 25 rows, it's really condensed representation of what's happening in a computer.
zh: 当你看着基本的终端,那个 80 列 25 行的黑盒子,它是对计算机中正在发生的事情的一种非常浓缩的表示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every byte, every character there is optimized over 40 years to convey only the most important information.
zh: 那里的每一个字节、每一个字符都经过了 40 年的优化,只传达最重要的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really optimized for people, but it turns out agents like this as well.
zh: 所以它真的是为人类优化的,但事实证明智能体也很喜欢这种形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And agents actually know Shell by heart.
zh: 而且智能体实际上把 Shell 背得滚瓜烂熟。

speaker: Unknown
en: They really know how to call CLI commands, how to pipe them.
zh: 它们真的知道如何调用 CLI 命令,如何用管道连接它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They really know how to use the Shell well, because they have seen it in so much training data.
zh: 它们真的知道如何把 Shell 用好,因为它们在如此多的训练数据中见过这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus, for AI labs, you can actually synthesize infinite amount of training data from using Shell.
zh: 此外,对于 AI 实验室来说,你实际上可以从使用 Shell 中合成无限的训练数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just pipe different commands together, explore the commands, extract information from your manual pages, and basically feed this all to the models.
zh: 你可以把不同的命令用管道连在一起,探索这些命令,从手册页中提取信息,然后基本上把这一切都喂给模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they know the Shell really, really well.
zh: 所以它们对 Shell 非常、非常熟悉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But CLIs are a local black box with no standard out and transport protocol.
zh: 但 CLI 是一个没有标准输出和传输协议的本地黑盒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, I mean, they are literally a black box.
zh: 所以基本上,我的意思是,它们字面意义上就是一个黑盒。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a black terminal thing, right?
zh: 它是一个黑色的终端玩意儿,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't see what's happening inside.
zh: 而且你看不到里面发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, if you wanted to like, you know, instrument like this, like CLIs in your enterprise, you would have to sort of like introspect the protocol and like, oh, are they using API or WebSockets or, you know, you don't know.
zh: 比如说，如果你想给你的企业里的这些 CLI 做插桩监测，你就得去内省这个协议，比如，哦，他们用的是 API 还是 WebSockets，还是什么，你不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot inject credentials into that.
zh: 你没法往里面注入凭证。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, CLIs are great for local interface.
zh: 所以基本上，CLI 很适合本地接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for remote access, MCP is better.
zh: 但对于远程访问，MCP 更好。

en: I mean, I have to see some agent using CLI connectors.
zh: 我是说，我还没见过哪个智能体在用 CLI 连接器。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't exist because it doesn't make sense.

speaker: Unknown
en: You have MCP connectors.
zh: 你有 MCP 连接器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how about we use MCP for standard remote access and CLI for local agent access, local agent interface with all the goodies that I described?
zh: 那么，我们用 MCP 做标准的远程访问，用 CLI 做本地智能体访问、本地智能体接口，并保留我描述的那些好处，怎么样？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这样的话，你就能提供 MCP 的所有协议特性，

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically the full complexity of MCP is hidden behind single tool call, Bash, and you don't need to worry about the sessions, authorization, all out, nothing.
zh: 所以基本上，MCP 的全部复杂性都藏在单个工具调用 Bash 背后，你不需要操心会话、授权，什么都不用管。

speaker: Unknown
en: So ladies and gentlemen, let me introduce you MCPC, which is like our universal CLI client for MCP.
zh: 那么，女士们先生们，让我向你们介绍 MCPC，这是我们的 MCP 通用 CLI 客户端。

speaker: Unknown
en: This started as a hobby project during December, also known as Winter of Claude.
zh: 这个项目始于十二月的一个业余项目，那个月也被称为「Claude 之冬」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from a hobby project, it actually evolved into probably the most feature-rich MCPC-like line on the market.
zh: 从一个业余项目，它实际上演化成了可能是市面上功能最丰富的 MCPC 类命令行工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can install it through NPM or BAN.
zh: 你可以通过 NPM 或 BAN 安装它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how it works, right?
zh: 那么它是怎么工作的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the design goes for MCPC, where, hey, we really want to support everything the MCP protocol has to offer.
zh: MCPC 的设计理念是，嘿，我们真的想支持 MCP 协议提供的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, tasks, resources, prompts, basically everything, right?
zh: 你知道，任务、资源、提示，基本上是一切，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And maximum compatibility to make it really easy to run anywhere, anytime.
zh: 以及最大的兼容性，让它真的可以随时随地轻松运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: MCP is like super lightweight.
zh: MCP 非常轻量。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is no LLM.
zh: 没有 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a wrapper, it's a CLI wrapper over the MCP protocol that sort of like abstracts away the protocol thing, but nothing else.
zh: 它只是一个包装器，是 MCP 协议之上的一个 CLI 包装器，把协议那些东西抽象掉了，仅此而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very, it's supposed to be easy to use for both agents and humans, obviously, and
zh: 它显然应该对智能体和人类都易于使用，而且

speaker: Unknown

zh: 它需要从头到尾支持 code mode。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, every command in MCPC has an option to run with dash dash JSON, which returns just pure JSON representation of the data.
zh: 实际上，MCPC 里每条命令都有一个选项可以用 dash dash JSON 运行，它只返回数据的纯 JSON 表示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, MCP specification compliant.
zh: 再说一次，符合 MCP 规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually, you can compose the different CLI calls together with tools like JQ, pipe them together, and really build sequences of tools, of tool calls in code.
zh: 所以实际上，你可以用 JQ 这类工具把不同的 CLI 调用组合起来，用管道串起来，真正地在代码里构建工具调用的序列。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'll show you how it looks like, just a quick demo.

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, let me connect to a local server.

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, no, no, no.

speaker: Unknown
en: So it supports STD.io, which is like the local processes running on your computer.

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say apify MCP server.
zh: 比如说 apify MCP 服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: It opens a browser where I run authentication.

speaker: Unknown
en: So just like pick some...

speaker: Unknown
en: Pick some account.
zh: 选择某个账号。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now the MCPC is logged in and basically it's securely saved the credentials into your local OS keychain so we can now use them to connect securely to different resources.

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me connect to Appify MCP server.

en: All right.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: MCP supports it, of course.

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it can release the tools.

speaker: Unknown
en: Available commands, and so on.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So I can try another command.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: In the background, and then eventually I can get the results.

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can get it right away in your browser.
zh: 而且你可以在浏览器中立即获取它。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 使用 CLI、MCP、MCPC 或其他什么工具哪个更有效？

zh: 所以实际上,这些测试还处于相当早期的阶段,不过,如果你来看看并做出贡献,我会很高兴。

en: So please stop saying CLI is better than MCP because MCP plus CLI is the best.
zh: 所以请不要再说什么 CLI 比 MCP 好了,因为 MCP 加 CLI 才是最好的。
